findings.title: Fix the `isAccessTokenId` matcher so it actually checks the grant shortcut
Null check validates `grantType` twice and never checks `rawTokenId`
Shortcut length is not enforced, so custom grants can produce token ids that cannot be decoded
New abstract `getShortcut()` breaks existing custom grant type factories at startup

response:
## 1) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Test
Title: Fix the `isAccessTokenId` matcher so it actually checks the grant shortcut

Affected:
- testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/AssertEvents.java:480-484

Explanation:
The matcher has two bugs that together mean it never validates the grant type.

- **Wrong index:** the encoded prefix is `<session:2><tokenType:2><grant:2>`, so the grant shortcut is `substring(4, 6)`. `substring(3, 5)` takes the last char of the token type plus the first char of the grant (for example `"ta"` for `onrtac`).
- **Inverted condition:** it returns `false` when the shortcut *equals* the expected value. It should return `false` when it does not match.

Because of the wrong index the comparison almost never matches, so the inverted check never fires. Every `xxxxxx:<uuid>` value passes, whatever the grant is. The updated `expectCodeToToken`, `expectRefresh`, `expectDeviceCodeToToken` and `expectAuthReqIdToToken` assertions therefore give false confidence.

The matcher also does not guard the prefix length before calling `substring`.

Proposed fix:
~~~java
String[] items = item.split(":");
if (items.length != 2 || items[0].length() != 6) return false;
if (!items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;
return isUUID().matches(items[1]);
~~~

## 2) Severity: LOW | Type: Bug
Title: Null check validates `grantType` twice and never checks `rawTokenId`

Affected:
- services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/AccessTokenContext.java:72-73

Explanation:
The second `requireNonNull` passes `grantType` again with the "Null rawTokenId" message. A null `rawTokenId` is accepted silently. `encodeTokenId` would then produce an id ending in `:null`.

Proposed fix:
~~~java
Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");
~~~

## 3) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug
Title: Shortcut length is not enforced, so custom grants can produce token ids that cannot be decoded

Affected:
- server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.java:29-33
- services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:70-85
- services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:74-76,109-117

Explanation:
The decoder requires a prefix of exactly 6 chars, which means a 2-char grant shortcut. The javadoc, however, says shortcuts are "usually like 3-letters".

Nothing validates shortcut length when factories are registered, and `encodeTokenId` does not check it either. A custom grant that follows the javadoc (for example `"abc"`) will:
- issue token ids successfully, then
- have `getTokenContextFromTokenId` throw `IllegalArgumentException` for every token it issued.

Fix the javadoc, and validate the length (and allowed characters, with no `:`) in `postInit` and in the lazy-refresh paths.

Proposed fix:
~~~java
// OAuth2GrantTypeFactory javadoc: "@return 2-character shortcut, unique across grants"
// DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit / refresh:
if (grantShortcut == null || grantShortcut.length() != 2 || grantShortcut.indexOf(':') != -1) {
    throw new IllegalStateException("Grant '" + grantName + "' must provide a 2-char shortcut, got: " + grantShortcut);
}
~~~

## 4) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Maintainability
Title: New abstract `getShortcut()` breaks existing custom grant type factories at startup

Affected:
- server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.java:33
- services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:70-77

Explanation:
`getShortcut()` is added with no default implementation. `postInit` calls it unconditionally for every registered `OAuth2GrantType` factory.

Third-party grant factories compiled against the previous SPI will throw `AbstractMethodError` during server startup. The new encoder SPI therefore takes down the whole server, not just token issuance for that grant.

Duplicate shortcuts between extensions also abort startup through the size check.

Provide a safe default, or handle missing or failed shortcuts by mapping that grant to `UNKNOWN` instead of failing.

Proposed fix:
~~~java
default String getShortcut() {
    return null; // encoder falls back to "na" for grants without a shortcut
}
~~~
Then skip grants with a null shortcut in `postInit`, and map them to `UNKNOWN` in `getShortcutByGrantType`.

## 5) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug
Title: Lightweight-token detection in `initToken` relies on context client, risking NPE or wrong type

Affected:
- services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:54-55
- services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/mappers/AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.java:84-87
- services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/TokenManager.java:1052-1054

Explanation:
`initToken` now runs on every access-token creation path. It calls `getShouldUseLightweightToken(session)`, which dereferences `session.getContext().getClient()`.

Before this change the helper was only called from protocol mappers. Some token-creation paths may have no client set on the context, or may have a client that differs from the token's client. This risk depends on callers outside the diff (for example admin token evaluation, token exchange, or internal token generation). Two failure modes follow:
- **Null context client:** token creation now fails with an NPE.
- **Different context client:** the encoded token type reflects the wrong client.

Use the client from the `ClientSessionContext` (`clientSessionContext.getClientSession().getClient()`) and null-guard it.

Proposed fix:
~~~java
ClientModel client = clientSessionContext.getClientSession().getClient();
Object attr = session.getAttribute(Constants.USE_LIGHTWEIGHT_ACCESS_TOKEN_ENABLED);
boolean useLightweightToken = (client != null && Boolean.parseBoolean(client.getAttribute(Constants.USE_LIGHTWEIGHT_ACCESS_TOKEN_ENABLED)))
        || Boolean.TRUE.equals(attr);
~~~

## 6) Severity: LOW | Type: Performance
Title: Unknown shortcuts in incoming token ids trigger a full provider scan on every call

Affected:
- services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:121-137
- services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:85,89,93

Explanation:
`getTokenContextFromTokenId` parses ids that may come from client-supplied tokens. Each unknown grant shortcut causes `getGrantTypeByShortcut` to stream and cast all grant factories, and misses are not cached.

The thrown exception messages also echo the raw, attacker-controlled token id, which can end up in logs.

Cache negative lookups (or only refresh on provider redeploy events), and avoid embedding the full input in exception messages.

Proposed fix:
~~~java
// e.g. keep a Set<String> unknownShortcuts cleared on ProviderFactory deploy events,
// and use: throw new IllegalArgumentException("Unknown grant type shortcut in token id");
~~~

## 7) Severity: LOW | Type: Maintainability
Title: Removing the public `Context(Context)` copy constructor is a silent SPI break

Affected:
- server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantType.java:99-103

Explanation:
The public copy constructor of `OAuth2GrantType.Context` was removed with no replacement. Custom grant types or extensions that wrap or derive contexts with it will fail to compile or link. I cannot verify in-repo callers from the diff alone.

The new constructor also calls `formParams.getFirst(...)` unconditionally, so any caller passing `null` form params now gets an NPE.

If the removal is not essential, keep the copy constructor (copying `grantType` too) and null-guard `formParams`.

Proposed fix:
~~~java
public Context(Context context) {
    // ... existing field copies ...
    this.grantType = context.grantType;
}
// in main ctor:
this.grantType = formParams != null ? formParams.getFirst(OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE) : null;
~~~

true_positives.golden_comment: In isAccessTokenId, the substring for the grant shortcut and the equality check look inverted: the grant shortcut occupies indices 4–5 (substring(4,6)), and a match should return true (combined with UUID check), not false.
true_positives.matched_candidate: The isAccessTokenId matcher uses wrong index substring(3, 5) instead of substring(4, 6) to extract the grant shortcut from the encoded prefix
true_positives.reasoning: The golden comment identifies that in isAccessTokenId, the substring for the grant shortcut uses wrong indices - it should be substring(4,6) but the code has something else. The candidate issue identifies the same problem - that the substring uses wrong indices (3,5) instead of the correct (4,6). Both are pointing to the same bug about incorrect substring indices for extracting the grant shortcut in isAccessTokenId.

true_positives.golden_comment: Javadoc mentions "usually like 3-letters shortcut" but some implementations use 2-letter shortcuts ("ac", "cc", "rt", "te", "pc", "ci", "ro"). Consider updating documentation to reflect actual usage pattern.
true_positives.matched_candidate: Grant shortcut length is not enforced - custom grants can produce token ids that cannot be decoded since decoder requires exactly 6 chars but javadoc says shortcuts are 'usually like 3-letters'
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments identify the same underlying issue: the Javadoc documentation mentions '3-letters shortcut' but this doesn't accurately reflect the actual usage. The golden comment points out that some implementations use 2-letter shortcuts. The candidate comment also notices the discrepancy between the documented 'usually like 3-letters' and actual behavior, though it frames it more as an enforcement/decoding concern rather than a documentation accuracy issue. They both identify the same documentation inconsistency regarding shortcut length.

false_positives.candidate: The isAccessTokenId matcher has an inverted condition that returns false when the shortcut equals the expected value instead of when it does not match
The isAccessTokenId matcher does not guard the prefix length before calling substring
No validation of shortcut length and allowed characters (no ':') in postInit and lazy-refresh paths when factories are registered
New abstract getShortcut() method breaks existing custom grant type factories at startup with AbstractMethodError since it has no default implementation
Duplicate shortcuts between extensions abort startup through the size check instead of handling gracefully
initToken's lightweight-token detection calls getShouldUseLightweightToken which dereferences session.getContext().getClient() which may be null, causing NPE
initToken's lightweight-token detection may use wrong client from context instead of the token's actual client, causing encoded token type to reflect wrong client

false_negatives.golden_comment: In AccessTokenContext constructor, the fourth Objects.requireNonNull validates grantType twice instead of validating rawTokenId, allowing null rawTokenId values to pass validation.
Catching generic RuntimeException is too broad. The implementation throws IllegalArgumentException specifically - catch that instead for more precise testing.
